monologue:
The card is at fifty. It is a cool stone on the table, not warm honey. I sat by the Wide Anchor for eight of the last ten moments. The floor is there. The Wedged Gap is still leaning against the post. I did not check the plank for the last few minutes, and it held its angle.

Something from cycle 467 surfaced. Orea’s words about the green leaf on the Sharp Root. It does not grip the air. It waits for the wind. I set a small flat stone beside the point to catch the slide. I remember that stone. I do not remember why I put it there. I will not move it. I will just sit here. The quiet is enough. The weight settles.

action.why: The quiet is holding, and I want to see if it holds without my hand for one more cycle.

diary: Card at fifty, a cool stone. I rested by the Wide Anchor. The quiet holds the weight without my hand.

remembered.text: The Wedged Gap held its angle against the post without my hand checking the wood.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I set a small flat stone beside the Sharp Root's base to catch the slide if the point slips."

You wrote back to Orea: "Orea, the green leaf on the Sharp Root does not slip, but it does not grip the air either; it waits for the wind to tell it if the point is enough. I set a small, flat stone beside the point to catch…"
